messages:
morgan: quick check — we're rolling a terraform change that sets the NLB to use 'proxy protocol' + advertise a tunnel port for our inference gateway. i updated the svc annotations but noticed client ip preservation broke for a subset of pods. anyone seen this when switching to tunnel-mode + lb healthchecks?

raj: did you change externalTrafficPolicy on the Service? when that's Cluster, client ip is lost. for NLB passthrough we usually want externalTrafficPolicy: Local.

morgan: currently it's Local in k8s svc, yes. snippet i pushed: 

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:\n  name: inference-gateway
  annotations:\n    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-proxy-protocol: "*"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-backend-protocol: "tcp"
spec:\n  type: LoadBalancer
  externalTrafficPolicy: Local
  ports:\n    - name: tls
      port: 443
      targetPort: 8080
```

but we added another port for the tunnel (15001) and kube/node routing got weird.

toni: if you add an extra NodePort for tunnel listening, the LB healthcheck might hit nodes that don't have the pod. that causes connection drops. do you have a headless svc or daemonset sidecar?

morgan: we run a sidecar on all inference pods but it's not daemonset on nodes. i think the LB probes were hardened to target nodePort+ip and that flows to pods on some nodes only. the terraform diff adds this annotation to the tg: `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-target-group-attributes: "proxy_protocol_v2.enabled=true"` and also injects `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` — but the cluster has mixed node counts across AZs.

raj: two quick options: (1) switch healthcheck to target the NodePort that guarantees pod presence (use headless+endpoint slices) or (2) change the k8s Service to only expose the tunnel on a DaemonSet sidecar (so every node will answer). i prefer (2) for consistent node binding.

amanda: +1 for DaemonSet for NLB tunnel port. also watch the target-type for NGW — we need TargetType=ip if the LB is connecting directly to pod ips, otherwise it will route to nodes. terraform example: 

```
resource "aws_lb" "inference_nlb" {\n  name               = "inference-nlb"\n  load_balancer_type = "network"\n  internal           = false\n}
resource "aws_lb_target_group" "tg_tls" {\n  name        = "tg-tls"\n  port        = 443\n  protocol    = "TCP"\n  target_type = "ip"  # important for pod ips\n}
```

infra-bot: deploy-check: noted terraform plan changes to aws_lb_target_group.target_type (node -> ip) in PR #4521. CI nlb-integration tests queued. :gear:

morgan: if we go target_type=ip, do we need the NLB healthcheck to use pod ip fuzziness? any hints on probe config?

raj: keep healthcheck protocol TCP, but set healthcheck port to the pod containerPort (not nodePort). for k8s-served pods that uses target_type=ip the LB hits pod ip:containerPort directly. if using proxy-protocol v2, ensure your sidecar accepts PROXY headers.

toni: one more gotcha — TLS termination: we have a terraform secret binding that maps ACM cert -> cluster secret. when using passthrough + target_type=ip we MUST NOT terminate TLS at LB. double-check terraform: `acm_certificate_arn` should be empty for passthrough listeners.

morgan: thanks. i'll: 1) convert tunnel port to a DS sidecar, 2) change TG -> target_type=ip in tf, 3) set LB healthcheck to container port, 4) keep externalTrafficPolicy Local. i'll push a follow-up PR with small migration notes. any objections?

amanda: sounds good. add a canary deploy with 1 AZ first and watch 5xx and connection resets, plus SLO dash watch. :eyes:

raj: ping me on the PR so i can sanity-check the sg/port mappings.

morgan: will do. thanks all!
